swot.point: A GI-registered double-ikat technique in which the yarn is tied and dyed to the motif before weaving, held as a living skill by all twenty participants across four villages. It cannot be reproduced on a power loom, and the survey found no counterfeit that came close on the reverse face.
supportedBy: Ms. Shreya Kulkarni, buying head, Tvaksati Design Studio, Bengaluru
Smt. Rina Mohanty, stall manager, Utkal Vastra craft counter

swot.point: The entire value chain — motif drafting, tying, dyeing, warping and weaving — sits inside Barpali under one co-operative society, so a change of product can be executed end to end without bringing in an outside vendor or a job worker.
supportedBy: Sri Prafulla Kumar Sahoo, proprietor, Sahoo Handloom Stores
Ms. Shreya Kulkarni, buying head, Tvaksati Design Studio, Bengaluru
Smt. Anita Das, Procurement Officer (Handloom), Boyanika
Sri Rajesh Bothra, partner, export merchant house, Kolkata

swot.point: The craft is already known to the buyer by name, which removes the cost of introducing an unfamiliar product. Recognition is not what has to be built; only the format has to change.
supportedBy: Smt. Anita Das, Procurement Officer (Handloom), Boyanika
Smt. Rina Mohanty, stall manager, Utkal Vastra craft counter

swot.point: The product range is effectively a single article. Almost everything the cluster offers is a saree, so it is absent from the gifting and home shelf where the turnover is, and it has no answer for a buyer who does not wear one.
supportedBy: Sri Rajesh Bothra, partner, export merchant house, Kolkata

swot.point: The production cycle is long and the working capital is locked up for the whole of it — forty-five to seventy days per saree against a unit realisation of ₹2,800 to ₹6,500, which leaves the artisan waiting for two months to be paid for one piece.
supportedBy: Ms. Shreya Kulkarni, buying head, Tvaksati Design Studio, Bengaluru
Smt. Rina Mohanty, stall manager, Utkal Vastra craft counter
Smt. Anita Das, Procurement Officer (Handloom), Boyanika

swot.point: Colour is not held across dye lots because dyeing is done household by household with dyestuff bought in small quantities and no written recipe. Institutional and export buyers named this, not price or design, as the single reason they do not place repeat orders.
supportedBy: Ms. Shreya Kulkarni, buying head, Tvaksati Design Studio, Bengaluru
Smt. Anita Das, Procurement Officer (Handloom), Boyanika
Sri Rajesh Bothra, partner, export merchant house, Kolkata
Sri Prafulla Kumar Sahoo, proprietor, Sahoo Handloom Stores

swot.point: An empty sub-₹2,000 gifting and home-linen shelf in every market surveyed, which retailers are currently filling with printed goods from outside the State for want of an Odia alternative.
supportedBy: Sri Prafulla Kumar Sahoo, proprietor, Sahoo Handloom Stores

swot.point: A younger urban buyer who rejects the saree but responds strongly to the same motif on a neutral ground in a smaller scale, opening a segment the cluster has never served.
supportedBy: Smt. Rina Mohanty, stall manager, Utkal Vastra craft counter

swot.point: Two institutional buyers are ready to commit to orders on conditions the cluster can meet within this workshop — a written dye recipe, colour matching across a lot and a stated delivery calendar.
supportedBy: Smt. Anita Das, Procurement Officer (Handloom), Boyanika
Sri Rajesh Bothra, partner, export merchant house, Kolkata
Ms. Shreya Kulkarni, buying head, Tvaksati Design Studio, Bengaluru
Smt. Rina Mohanty, stall manager, Utkal Vastra craft counter

swot.point: Screen-printed power-loom imitation of the ikat blur, sold at a fifth of the handwoven price, occupies the exact shelf slot and price expectation the new range is aimed at, and it conditions the buyer to a price the craft can never meet.
supportedBy: Smt. Rina Mohanty, stall manager, Utkal Vastra craft counter
Sri Prafulla Kumar Sahoo, proprietor, Sahoo Handloom Stores

swot.point: Other genuine ikat clusters are already occupying the diversified formats in Odisha's own retail space, and they have moved first. Pochampally is selling table linen in Bhubaneswar and Nuapatna is holding the premium stole shelf at Boyanika.
supportedBy: Smt. Rina Mohanty, stall manager, Utkal Vastra craft counter
Smt. Anita Das, Procurement Officer (Handloom), Boyanika
Sri Prafulla Kumar Sahoo, proprietor, Sahoo Handloom Stores
Sri Rajesh Bothra, partner, export merchant house, Kolkata

swot.point: The tying skill is ageing and thinning. Tying is the slowest operation and the scarcest capacity in the cluster, and if younger hands continue to leave for wage work, any order growth will run into a constraint that cannot be purchased or hired quickly.
supportedBy: Sri Prafulla Kumar Sahoo, proprietor, Sahoo Handloom Stores
Sri Rajesh Bothra, partner, export merchant house, Kolkata
